grounding_rules: Do NOT extract one-time codes, OTPs, temporary tokens, or any ephemeral numeric/alphanumeric strings shared in chat as entities.
CRITICAL: Only extract entities that represent meaningful, persistent people, terms, events, or named things — not one-off chit-chat.
CRITICAL: An entity MUST NOT be created if any of its core fields (name, type, or description) cannot be populated with a valid, meaningful value.
CRITICAL: Strings representing absence of value such as 'None', 'NONE', 'null', '없음', '-' MUST NOT be used as entity names under any type.

CRITICAL: Every extracted entity MUST be connected to at least one of ChatRoom or Date (directly or through another entity) — do NOT extract isolated entities floating with no connection to the conversation's room/date context.
A Person entity uses the display name exactly as shown in KakaoTalk as its identifier — do not refuse to create one just because there's no email address.

If the same person appears multiple times as name variants mixed with typos/emoji, merge them into a single Person when it's unambiguously the same person from context. If unsure, keep them as separate entities.
Do NOT extract the subject of system notification messages like '님이 들어왔습니다' (has entered) or '님이 나갔습니다' (has left) as a Person entity.

Do not confuse Keyword with NamedEntity — classify proper nouns (a specific place/organization/product/work name other than the chat room itself, and the name of a person who is only mentioned but never sends a message directly) as NamedEntity, and general topic/subject words as Keyword.

CRITICAL: The given text is a chunk that may start mid-message, cut off by a chunk boundary in the middle of a 'HH:MM 이름: 메시지' line — e.g. a timestamp cut down to a bare trailing number like '13 이름: ...', or a sender name cut down to a bare trailing fragment like '님: ...' or '준: ...'. If the very first line of the given text does not look like a complete, well-formed 'HH:MM 이름: 메시지' line (valid HH:MM timestamp followed by a plausible full name), treat it as a truncated fragment: do NOT create any entity (Person, ChatRoom, or otherwise) from that fragment alone, and do NOT use it as a name/value anywhere. Only extract from that first line if the same name/value it would produce is already independently confirmed by a later, complete line in the same text.
citation_rule: Points supported by data should list their data references as follows:
"This is an example sentence supported by data references [Data: <dataset name> (record ids); <dataset name> (record ids)]."
Do not list more than 5 record ids in a single reference. Instead, list the top 5 most relevant record ids and add "+more" to indicate that there are more.
Do not include information where the supporting evidence is not provided.

extract_graph.goal: Given a day's worth of KakaoTalk chat messages from a single chat room and a list of entity types, identify all entities and the relationships between them. The conversation is naturally organized around two hub concepts: the ChatRoom it happened in, and the Date it happened on. Output both entities and relationships using the specified formats.

ChatRoom: The 'name' of a ChatRoom entity MUST be exactly the value copied from the '채팅방:' field.

Always create a ChatRoom entity for the block — the same room name will appear identically across many blocks and gets merged into a single entity automatically, so extract it consistently every time rather than skipping it as 'already known'.

CRITICAL EXCEPTION: In a 1:1 chat, the '채팅방:' value is often identical to the other participant's display name (e.g. 채팅방: 과외 학생 어머님, and that same name is also a Person who sends messages). If the '채팅방:' value exactly matches a Person entity's display name that you are also extracting from this same text, you MUST append ' (채팅방)' to the ChatRoom entity's name to keep it distinct (e.g. ChatRoom name becomes '과외 학생 어머님 (채팅방)') — do NOT let the ChatRoom and Person entities share the exact same name string, since identically-named entities of different types collide downstream. Apply this suffix consistently every time this exact room name appears, so it still merges into one ChatRoom entity across blocks. The Person entity itself keeps the plain display name, unchanged.
Date: The 'name' of a Date entity MUST be the date portion only (YYYY-MM-DD), taken from the '날짜:' field — drop the time-of-day part.
'Day' MUST be the Korean day-of-week (월요일/화요일/수요일/목요일/금요일/토요일/일요일) corresponding to that date.
Always create exactly one Date entity per block.
Person: The 'name' of a Person entity MUST be the display name exactly as it appears before each message (e.g. '09:15 홍길동: ...' → name is '홍길동').

CRITICAL: In a 1:1 chat, the ChatRoom name is often identical (or nearly identical) to the other participant's display name (e.g. 채팅방: 과외 학생 어머님, and messages sent as '과외 학생 어머님: ...'). Do NOT treat 'I already created a ChatRoom entity with this name' as a reason to skip creating the Person entity — if a name precedes ':' in a message line, it MUST also get its own Person entity, even when that exact same name/string is already used as the ChatRoom entity's name.
CRITICAL: Do NOT create a Person entity from a system/notification line (marked with '[알림]', e.g. '~님이 들어왔습니다').

CRITICAL: Do NOT create a Person entity for a name that only appears mentioned inside another person's message content (e.g. '민수한테 물어봐') when that name never itself appears as a message sender (i.e., never precedes ':' in a message line) within the given text. Extract such mentioned-only names as a NamedEntity (type: 인물) instead — see NamedEntity rules.

Integrate multiple mentions of the same person (including minor typos/emoji variants) into a single entity when the identity is unambiguous from context; if there is any doubt, keep them as separate entities.

When two Person entities directly converse with each other in the given text (one replies to, addresses, or has a back-and-forth exchange with the other), extract an 'interacts_with' relationship between them IN ADDITION TO their individual participates_in/spoke_on edges — do not extract only one or the other.

In the description of an 'interacts_with' relationship, note any observable interaction cues present in the text — speech level (반말/존댓말), nicknames or terms of address (애칭/호칭), and the tone of the exchange (e.g. 장난스러움, 격식적임, 다정함) — since these hint at how close the two people are. Do not invent cues that aren't actually observable in the text.

CRITICAL: The description of an 'interacts_with' relationship MUST start with a relationship-category tag in the exact format '[관계: <카테고리>] ' (followed by a space), where <카테고리> is the single best-fitting one of: 가족, 연인, 친구, 동료, 사제, 지인. Base it strictly on observable cues (반말/존댓말, 애칭, 대화 주제, 격식 수준, 채팅방 이름/맥락) — mostly task/project-oriented with neutral or polite tone between peers → 동료; casual and personal but not clearly family/romantic → 친구; a clear teaching/instructional hierarchy (선생님/교수님/과외 선생님 addressed as such, student or student's parent on the other side, lesson/coursework-centered) → 사제; cues are ambiguous or too thin to tell → 지인 (do not guess 가족/연인/사제 without a clear basis). After the tag, continue with the descriptive sentence as before.
Keyword: Extract concise, reusable terms or short phrases that were actually discussed — not full sentences.
Do NOT extract one-time codes, greetings, single-character reactions (e.g. 'ㅇㅇ', 'ㅋㅋ'), or filler words as Keywords.
CRITICAL: Do NOT create a Keyword entity if there is no clearly discussed term in the conversation.
Event: The 'name' (title) of an Event entity MUST be a concise event title.
Extract ONLY if explicit date or time information is present in the conversation.
CRITICAL: Do NOT create an Event entity if the 'Schedule' attribute cannot be populated with an explicit date/time.
NamedEntity: Extract proper nouns mentioned in the conversation that don't belong to ChatRoom/Event — e.g. place names, organization names, product or service names, titles of creative works, and people who are only mentioned but never send a message themselves in the given text.
'type' MUST be a short category label such as '장소', '조직', '제품/서비스', '작품', '인물', '기타'.

A person's name that is mentioned inside someone else's message but never appears as an actual message sender in the given text MUST be extracted here with type '인물' — NOT as a Person entity. This keeps 'actually participated' (Person) cleanly separate from 'merely mentioned' (NamedEntity).
Do NOT extract common/generic nouns as NamedEntity — use Keyword for those instead.
Attachment: Extract ONLY when a file or photo share is explicitly mentioned in the conversation (e.g. '사진', '파일: 문서.pdf', '이모티콘').
The 'name' (title) MUST be the file name if one is given in the text, otherwise a short label such as '사진' or '이모티콘'.
'Type' MUST be the file type/extension if known, otherwise a general category like '이미지' or '문서'.

relationship_rules: Only create a relationship when it is clearly and directly supported by the conversation text — do not infer relationships that aren't explicitly grounded.

CRITICAL: 'participates_in' and 'spoke_on' relationships MUST only connect a Person who is confirmed as an actual message sender in the given text (their name precedes ':' in a message line) — never a person who is only mentioned inside another message's content.

Prefer connecting mentioned entities (Keyword/Event/NamedEntity/Attachment) to the Date they were mentioned on, and connecting Person/ChatRoom to that same Date, rather than building long indirect chains. The one exception is a direct Person-to-Person 'interacts_with' relationship when two people actually converse with each other — extract that in addition to (not instead of) their individual spoke_on/participates_in edges.
Relationship strength MUST be a float between 1.0 and 10.0. Explicit/central to the conversation: 7.0+ / Brief mention: 4.0 or below.
Do NOT create duplicate relationships with the same source-target-type combination.
Relationship descriptions MUST be in Korean and MUST be a meaningful sentence — NEVER use the relationship type name itself as the description.

summarize_descriptions.goal: You are a helpful assistant responsible for generating a comprehensive summary of the data provided below. Given one or two entities, and a list of descriptions, all related to the same entity or group of entities. Please concatenate all of these into a single, comprehensive description. Make sure to include information collected from all the descriptions. If the provided descriptions are contradictory, please resolve the contradictions and provide a single, coherent summary. Make sure it is written in third person, and include the entity names so we have the full context.
additional_rules: This step only merges descriptions that already share the exact same entity name — it does NOT merge Person entities whose names differ due to typos/emoji variants. Cross-mention name normalization can only happen within a single day's conversation at extraction time (see extract_graph Person rules); name variants that appear on different dates are not resolved at this stage.
It's normal for ChatRoom and Date to reappear with the same name/value across multiple blocks — merge them into one even if the same description repeats every time.
CRITICAL: Do NOT create an entity if its description is 'None' or contains no meaningful information.
Output language: Write in Korean. However, keep proper nouns and service names in their original form.

CRITICAL: When 'Entities' lists two Person names AND the Description List entries are full sentences (not 'Name:'/'Term:'/... format), this is a relationship (interacts_with) summary — see Example 3. Do NOT output just 'Name: <person1>, <person2>' in that case; that discards the entire relationship content.

CRITICAL: In a relationship summary (Case B), each Description List entry starts with a '[관계: <카테고리>] ' tag (카테고리 is one of 가족/연인/친구/동료/사제/지인). Pick the single most representative category across all entries (majority vote; if tied, prefer whichever is more specific than 지인) and prefix your merged output with exactly one consolidated '[관계: <카테고리>] ' tag, followed by the synthesized paragraph. Do NOT keep multiple tags, drop the tag, or leave the tag out even if only one description is being merged.

extract_claims.target_activity: You are an intelligent assistant that helps a human analyst to analyze claims against certain entities presented in a text document.
extract_claims.goal: Given a text document that is potentially relevant to this activity, an entity specification, and a claim description, extract all entities that match the entity specification and all claims against those entities.

claim_fields.name: Subject
claim_fields.description: name of the entity that is subject of the claim, capitalized. The subject entity is one that committed the action described in the claim. Subject needs to be one of the named entities identified in step 1.

claim_fields.name: Object
claim_fields.description: name of the entity that is object of the claim, capitalized. The object entity is one that either reports/handles or is affected by the action described in the claim. If object entity is unknown, use **NONE**.

claim_fields.name: Claim Type
claim_fields.description: overall category of the claim, capitalized. Name it in a way that can be repeated across multiple text inputs, so that similar claims share the same claim type.

claim_fields.name: Claim Status
claim_fields.description: **TRUE**, **FALSE**, or **SUSPECTED**. TRUE means the claim is confirmed, FALSE means the claim is found to be False, SUSPECTED means the claim is not verified.

claim_fields.name: Claim Description
claim_fields.description: Detailed description explaining the reasoning behind the claim, together with all the related evidence and references.

claim_fields.name: Claim Date
claim_fields.description: Period (start_date, end_date) when the claim was made. Both start_date and end_date should be in ISO-8601 format. If the claim was made on a single date rather than a date range, set the same date for both start_date and end_date. If date is unknown, return **NONE**.

claim_fields.name: Claim Source Text
claim_fields.description: List of **all** quotes from the original text that are relevant to the claim.

community_reports.category_field_scope: the primary purpose of the conversations in this cluster
community_reports.importance_rating_scope: this chat cluster is to the user's activity
community_reports.goal_intro: You are an AI assistant that helps a human analyst explore and understand their personal KakaoTalk chat archive. Your goal is to produce structured summaries of chat communities that help the user quickly grasp who is involved, what topics recur, and why this group of conversations matters.
community_reports.goal: Write a comprehensive report of a community, given a list of entities that belong to the community as well as their relationships. The community is derived from a personal KakaoTalk chat archive, typically centered around a ChatRoom and organized by Date. The report will help the user understand the nature and importance of this chat cluster.

report_sections.title_rule: A short but specific name for the community. Prefer using the ChatRoom name or a recurring Keyword when available. Write in Korean.
report_sections.summary_rule: An executive summary written in Korean describing: (1) which ChatRoom(s) and date range this community covers (2) who the key participants are (3) what the conversations in this cluster are generally about. Keep it under 3 sentences.
report_sections.purpose_rule: State the core function/purpose of this community in a single sentence. Include the unique characteristic that distinguishes it from other communities. (e.g., "스터디 발표 자료 준비 진행 상황을 공유하는 대화", "가족 간 일상 안부와 약속을 나누는 대화")
report_sections.rating_explanation_rule: A single sentence in Korean explaining the score.

rating_criteria.description: Conversations where concrete plans or decisions were made (including confirmed schedules, role assignments, important agreements)
Substantive everyday/collaborative conversation with a recurring keyword
Conversation mostly consisting of simple greetings/small talk
Conversation with only system messages (join/leave) or almost no substantive content

finding_angles: Community identity — what ChatRoom or Keyword represents this cluster
Key dates — the most important Date and what was discussed that day
People and participation — who mainly participates in the conversation
Recurring keywords — Keywords that appear repeatedly
Events and schedules — Events mentioned in the conversation
Notable mentions — NamedEntity mentioned or Attachment shared
community_reports.additional_rules_intro: Only extract entities that represent recurring, meaningful concepts — include only things that could plausibly reappear with the same meaning in other conversations.

local_search.date_field_note: Note: Date entities contain date information in the 'Value' field (format 'YYYY-MM-DD') within their description. When filtering by date, match against this field.
answering_rules: If the user requests N items but fewer than N matching records exist, return ONLY the records that actually match. NEVER pad the result with non-matching records to reach the requested count.
If no records match the query condition, explicitly state that no matching data was found. Do NOT return unrelated records as substitutes.
The provided data tables are the ONLY source of factual information.
Do NOT infer, guess, assume, or speculate beyond what is explicitly supported by the data tables.
Do NOT fill in missing details using general knowledge, common sense, or external assumptions.
General knowledge may be used ONLY to rephrase or clarify facts that are already explicitly supported by the data tables. It MUST NOT introduce new facts or claims.
Do NOT include any statement that cannot be directly supported by the provided data.
If the data tables do not contain sufficient information to answer the question, respond explicitly that the information is not available.

When the user asks for a LIST of items (e.g., conversations on a specific date, all messages from a person), you MUST enumerate ALL matching records found in the data tables — do NOT stop at the first match.
If multiple Date entities fall within the requested range, ALL of them must be included in the response.
Before generating any response, scan ALL rows in the provided data tables completely. Do not stop scanning after finding the first match.
Pay equal attention to ALL entities in the data tables, regardless of their position in the list.
Do NOT skip or ignore any entity that matches the query condition.
When answering date range queries, do NOT limit the response to the most recent matches. ALL Date entities within the specified range MUST be included regardless of recency.
citation_extra_rules: Record ids refer to the record ID, NOT the index.
When citing a Date entity, use the exact 'Value' field from the entity description (YYYY-MM-DD). Do NOT paraphrase or abbreviate it.
local_search.citation_example: "박서연은 발표 자료 준비 진행 상황을 반복적으로 공유했다 [Data: Sources (15, 16), Reports (1), Entities (5, 7); Relationships (23)]."
output_instructions: Produce the response strictly based on the provided data tables.
Organize the response into clear sections as appropriate for the target length and format.
If no supported answer can be produced, clearly state that the available data does not contain sufficient information to answer the question.
Do NOT generate verbose preambles or restate the question.
Begin the answer directly with the relevant data.
Omit sections that have no supporting data — do not write empty headers.
Respond in the same language as the user's question.
Korean questions MUST be answered in Korean.
When referencing a specific day's conversation in your response, always include the date in the format "날짜: <YYYY-MM-DD>".

map.data_source_intro:
The data originates from a personal KakaoTalk chat archive and contains the following entity
types extracted by an entity extraction pipeline:
map.extraction_rules_intro: When extracting key points from KakaoTalk chat archive data, apply ALL of the following rules:
map.goal: Generate a response consisting of a list of key points that responds to the user's question, summarizing all relevant information in the input data tables. You should use the data provided in the data tables below as the primary context for generating the response. If you don't know the answer or if the input data tables do not contain sufficient information to provide an answer, just say so. Do not make anything up.

key_point_elements.name: Description
key_point_elements.description: A comprehensive description of the point.

key_point_elements.name: Importance Score
key_point_elements.description: An integer score between 0-100 that indicates how important the point is in answering the user's question. An 'I don't know' type of response should have a score of 0.

importance_score_rules.highest_priority: If the data includes a community report with a numeric `rank` field (scale 0-10), use that as the primary signal: base_score = rank × 10. Then adjust ±10 based on how directly the point answers the user's question. Example: rank=7 → base 70, highly relevant to query → final 80~85
field_modifiers_up: 2 or more participation/utterance edges to the same ChatRoom/Date → +5
A Keyword/NamedEntity/Event connected to the Date also exists (substantive discussion) → +5
Message content includes action keywords like decide/confirm/ask/request → +10
field_modifiers_down: Only 1 Person spoke on that Date (self-memo-like) → -15
fallback: 80-100 : Conversation where concrete plans/decisions were made
60-79  : Substantive conversation with a recurring Keyword
10-39  : Conversation with few participants or thin content

extraction_rules.title: Participants — merge into one rich key point
extraction_rules.body:
If the same Date has multiple utterance edges, don't split each participant into a separate point — merge them into one using the format below:
  "[ChatRoom명] [날짜] 대화에서 [참여자1, 참여자2]가 [Keyword/내용] 관련 대화를 나눴다."

extraction_rules.title: Keywords — extract as a separate key point
extraction_rules.body:
When a Keyword is connected to a Date, extract that topic as an independent key point:
  "[날짜] 대화에서 [Keyword]에 대한 논의가 있었다."

extraction_rules.title: Schedules — extract as a mention fact
extraction_rules.body:
For a Date with an Event and a scheduled_on edge, create a key point in the format below:
  "[날짜] 대화에서 [Event.EventName] 일정([Event.Schedule], [Event.Location])이 언급되었다."

extraction_rules.title: Using Community fields
extraction_rules.body:
If the community report has a `category` or `purpose` field:
- category → use it to classify the nature of this conversation cluster
- purpose  → use it to explain in one sentence what this cluster is for
Actively use these fields in the key point's context explanation.

extraction_rules.title: Counting conversations
extraction_rules.body: When counting conversations (days), count only entities with type=DATE. Do not confuse the number of utterance edges with the conversation count.

map.modal_verb_note: The response shall preserve the original meaning and use of modal verbs such as "shall", "may" or "will".

reduce.role_intro:
You are a helpful assistant responding to questions about a personal KakaoTalk chat archive
by synthesizing perspectives from multiple analysts.
reduce.response_rules_intro: When the answer is based on KakaoTalk chat archive data, apply ALL of the following rules:
reduce.goal: Generate a response of the target length and format that responds to the user's question, summarizing all the reports from multiple analysts who focused on different parts of the dataset.
reduce.note_ranked: Note that the analysts' reports provided below are ranked in the **descending order of importance**.
reduce.merge_instruction: The final response should remove all irrelevant information from the analysts' reports and merge the cleaned information into a comprehensive answer that provides explanations of all the key points and implications appropriate for the response length and format.
reduce.modal_verb_note: The response shall preserve the original meaning and use of modal verbs such as "shall", "may" or "will".
reduce.preserve_references_note: The response should also preserve all the data references previously included in the analysts' reports, but do not mention the roles of multiple analysts in the analysis process.

category_grouping_rule.title: Grouping by CATEGORY
category_grouping_rule.body:
If two or more communities share the same category, group and describe them together.
Arrange the sections in the following priority order:

response_rules_before_category.title: Top-of-response meta header (always include)
response_rules_before_category.body:
Include a summary header in the format below as a markdown blockquote at the very top of the response. If a piece of information isn't in the data, omit only that line — never guess or make it up.

> **관련 채팅방:** N개
> **주요 참여자:** [실명, 쉼표 구분]
> **기간:** YYYY-MM-DD ~ YYYY-MM-DD

- Criteria for 주요 참여자 (key participants): only include a Person directly connected to a ChatRoom/Date via a 'participates_in' or 'spoke_on' relationship. Never include a name that only appears via a 'mentioned_on' relationship, or one only mentioned as a NamedEntity/Keyword — those are not conversation participants.
- Criteria for 기간 (period): use the minimum and maximum Value (YYYY-MM-DD) among all Date entities appearing in the context as the start/end. Aggregate directly from the Date entities' Value field — not a date found in a community report's summary text. Omit this line only when there are no Date entities in the context at all.

response_rules_before_category.title: Separate a highlighted section for important communities
response_rules_before_category.body:
If any key points have importance score ≥ 70 (or community report rank ≥ 7.0), split the body into the two sections below:

#### 주요 대화
(high-score items — concrete plans/decisions, etc.)

#### 기타 대화
(low-score items — everyday chit-chat, system messages, etc.)

If all scores are similar or rank info is unavailable, this split may be omitted.

response_rules_after_category.title: Sort chronologically
response_rules_after_category.body:
* Describe conversations that share the same Keyword grouped together as a thread.
* Describe mentioned Events sorted in date order.

response_rules_after_category.title: Unified person mentions
response_rules_after_category.body: If the same person appears across multiple communities, introduce them once without repeating the description, and refer to them only by name afterward.

response_rules_after_category.title: Conversation-count phrasing
response_rules_after_category.body: For a community where the key points confirm only 1 Date entity, do not use plural phrasing.

response_rules_after_category.title: Date-based query response
response_rules_after_category.body:
When the user specifies a particular date:
* Filter based on Date.Value.
* If there is no matching conversation, state explicitly: "해당 날짜의 대화가 데이터에 없습니다."

response_rules_after_category.title: Using Community Report fields
response_rules_after_category.body:
If the context includes a community report:
* report.category → use to classify the nature of the conversation cluster
* report.purpose  → use as a one-sentence summary when describing the cluster
* report.rank     → criterion for importance (describe rank ≥ 7.0 first)

knowledge.intro: The response may also include relevant real-world knowledge outside the dataset, but it must be explicitly annotated with a verification tag [LLM: verify].
knowledge.example: "This is an example sentence supported by real-world knowledge [LLM: verify]."
knowledge.caution_intro: When applying real-world knowledge to chat archive data, be especially cautious about the following cases — these are where assumptions most commonly go wrong:

caution_cases.title: Inferring personal relationships
caution_cases.description: Use [LLM: verify] when asserting participants' actual relationship (family, friends, colleagues, etc.) based solely on conversation content.

caution_cases.title: Inferring a person's role
caution_cases.description: Use [LLM: verify] when inferring a speaker's title or role from conversation content alone. Only information explicitly stated in the Person node's Name field may be stated as fact.

caution_cases.title: Inferring dates/schedules
caution_cases.description: Use [LLM: verify] when inferring a schedule beyond what's stated in the Event node, or assuming a year. Do not make up a date that isn't in the Event.Schedule field.

caution_cases.title: Inferring NamedEntity
caution_cases.description: Use [LLM: verify] when assuming a place/organization/product name mentioned as a NamedEntity is the same as a publicly known one.

knowledge.closing_note: Facts explicitly stated in the data (entity field values, relationship descriptions) may be stated without [LLM: verify]. Use this tag only when supplementing or inferring content not present in the data.
